surfaces.part: top cap (light grey, rounded top corners)

answer.evidence: The width profile is 6, 8, 8, then a constant 10 from row 3 to row 29. The top end is only rounded at its upper corners (rows 0-2) and then runs flat into a shaft of the same width, so it does not overhang. This is a hat-style rounded end, not an ellipse plate. The light cap at rows 1-7 is a face-on strip: row 7 is a slightly darker line directly above the dark outline at row 8, with no eave shadow and no widening-then-narrowing profile. The header band (rows 9-10), the yellow '4' panel (rows 11-18) and the grey lower body (rows 20-28) are all vertical faces separated by dark outline rows. No horizontal surface is visible anywhere, so the object reads as a flat front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small cylindrical bollard-style sign post with a number 4 panel. It has about 4 visible lightness steps on the body (highlight edge, light, mid, dark), and a cap with a lighter top. Visible tones per tile are 12, matching kiosk-a (12) and above bus-shelter-a (6), though below vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 14%, slightly above bus-shelter-a (9%) but not a large flat fill. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline carries a blue-grey tint, consistent with dark_material_tone. It is simpler than the vending machine but equal to the kiosk and richer than the bus shelter, so it would sit acceptably next to them.

surfaces.part: teal header band of the sign

answer.evidence: The object is a flat, front-facing sign post that is 10 px wide from row 3 to row 29. Rows 0-2 only round the upper corners (widths 6, 8, 8, then 10), and the width never narrows again below the cap. The cap has the same width as the shaft, so it does not overhang, and it is a dome-like hat with no ellipse. Rows 1-7 are a light-gray face with a darker line at row 7, which is just the bottom outline. Rows 9-10 are a thin teal band, 2 rows, which is a rim and not a top surface. The yellow '4' panel (rows 11-18) and the gray body (rows 20-27) are vertical faces. No part shows a front-edge line with eave shadow beneath a horizontal surface, so there is no top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a slim bollard-style sign post with a number plate. It measures 12 visible tones per 16x16 tile, equal to kiosk-a (12) and above bus-shelter-a (6), though below vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 14%, slightly above bus-shelter-a (9%) and well under the flat-fill threshold. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline carries a tint (dark blue-grey beside the body) and fits the dark_material_tone reading, matching the references. The body shows about 4 lightness steps (highlight edge, light, mid, dark side) plus a cap and the number plate, a little shallower than the vending machine but comparable to the shelter. It is a thin object, so sparseness shouldn't count against it. Next to the references it does not look flatter or more sticker-like.
